newsitem.title: UK: T-bonds idle in London,seen slipping ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: T-bonds idle in London,seen slipping ahead of FOMC.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were steady in quiet London trade on Friday after an early tick down on the softer dollar, traders said.
Analysts expected little upside to the market ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting (FOMC), the prospect of which was keeping ivestors firmly sidelined.
"The Treasury market may have to make a concession between now and next Tuesday," said Phil Tyson, international economist at HSBC Markets here.
"So the additional upside to the market is limited given the scaling back of tightening expectations recently...and I would favour a downside bias ahead of the meeting."
By 0955 GMT, the 30-year T-bond was at 96-31 to yield 6.86 percent, from 97-00 in Tokyo and 96-30 at the New York close.
One dealer said there had been some demand for five-year paper, which was at 100-16, unchanged from Tokyo and up from 100-15 in New York.
"We took a little down trade early on because of the dollar, but trade is very light," the dealer added.
The dollar came under renewed pressure in early European trade after a bout of short covering overnight. By 1007 GMT, dollar/yen was at 115.40/50.
Tyson said he still expected the Fed to raise rates by a quarter point next Tuesday. He said Thursday's 31,000 drop in jobless claims suggested the U.S. labour market was fairly tight.
"So this leaves us comfortable with our expectation of a 25 basis point rise in interest rates next week."

Tyson said April housing starts data due at 1230 GMT would likely have little impact on the market. He expected the data to come in at 1.5 million, slightly higher than the consensus estimate of 1.43 million.
"There won't be any huge impact on the market, but it will help our view of a more downward bias to the market next Tuesday," he said.
The University of Michigan May consumer sentiment index is due at 1400 GMT. Forecasts were for a slight tick up to 101.6 from 101.4 previously.
By 1031 GMT, the June T-bond future was unchanged at 110-10 in automated trade.
